body.heading: Make your star frame
paragraphs: Your adult cuts a square window in a sheet of card. This is your star frame. Wait for a clear, dark night and lie on a blanket outside with your adult.
The darker the sky, the more stars you can see. Street lights hide the faint ones, so let your eyes get used to the dark for a few minutes first.

body.heading: Count inside the frame
paragraphs: Hold the frame up with straight arms and count every star inside the square. Write the number down or remember it.
Now point the frame at a different part of the sky and count again. Some squares are busy star cities. Some are quiet star villages.

body.heading: A sky full of numbers
paragraphs: Scientists estimate numbers in just this way — count a small patch carefully, then imagine the whole sky.
Nobody can count every star one by one. There are far too many. Your little square is a window into something enormous.

takeaway: Counting stars in one small square shows how the sky holds more stars than anyone could ever count.
materials: A sheet of card (an adult cuts the window)
safetyNotes: Only go out at night with an adult, in a safe place. Never look at the Sun — this is a night-time activity only.
screenFreeExtension: Sprinkle a pinch of salt on dark paper and count the 'stars' in a drawn square, just like the sky game.
